### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/spec`, touching **1** documentable anchor(s).

**1** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/data-modeling/analytics.mdx`  _(via ReportSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **60** of **215** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **155** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **155**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **100** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **136** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 8cbc3c0084a3c3c8ef5e59763ab3be96aa1a6f07` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `a3d2e127db18cec1aba60725844cb99b5471553a` — the merge of head `926cff321dbd78de2a834f22d21da3a05c9a8740` into base `8cbc3c0084a3c3c8ef5e59763ab3be96aa1a6f07`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin a3d2e127db18cec1aba60725844cb99b5471553a && git checkout a3d2e127db18cec1aba60725844cb99b5471553a
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 8cbc3c0084a3c3c8ef5e59763ab3be96aa1a6f07 926cff321dbd78de2a834f22d21da3a05c9a8740 && git checkout -B drift-repro 8cbc3c0084a3c3c8ef5e59763ab3be96aa1a6f07 && git merge --no-ff 926cff321dbd78de2a834f22d21da3a05c9a8740

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 8cbc3c0084a3c3c8ef5e59763ab3be96aa1a6f07
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 8cbc3c0084a3c3c8ef5e59763ab3be96aa1a6f07` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: 56/56 `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `926cff321dbd78de2a834f22d21da3a05c9a8740`

Isolated at-tier reviewer subagent, run by the `domain:spec` seat-4 session on the maintainer's instruction in that session (「帮我处理」, with the landing route chosen there); every one of its 56 transcript turns served at the tier the constant names. Adopted by the seat 2026-09-24T05:34Z. The record below is the reviewer's, unedited except the two header lines.


### ① Derived judgments

Inputs read: card #19822 body + all 4 comments (triage 5792313693, claim 5793125463, os-dev-report rounds 1 and 2), PR #19855 body/files/diff (`application/vnd.github.diff`), 1 issue comment (docs-drift bot), 0 review comments, 0 reviews, 42 check-runs at head, refs fetched (`origin/main` = `c1641868a3`, `refs/review/pr-19855` = `926cff321d`, merge-base `71ef2219886f26acbadc18849d92691040248b5e`). `git diff --stat 71ef221988 refs/review/pr-19855` = exactly the 4 files in `pulls/19855/files`; no ruling from a maintainer/director exists on the card, so the judge is the card's stated defect plus triage's first-step order (5792313693) and AGENTS.md.

1. **Accept-set: unchanged, correctly.** The only schema change is +10 entries in `ReportSchema.aliases` (`refs/review/pr-19855:packages/spec/src/ui/report.zod.ts:279-304`). An alias is consulted only from the `unrecognized_keys` path (`origin/main:packages/spec/src/shared/strict-object.ts:249-251`; `origin/main:packages/spec/src/shared/suggestions.zod.ts:479-480`, `const declared = aliases[aliasProbe(key)]; const guessed = declared ? undefined : findClosestMatches(...)`), so no key is accepted or refused differently. No shape key added/removed (shape at `:321-407`); no export changes, so no `.d.ts`/api-surface movement. Runtime effect is limited to the text of one existing `unrecognized_keys` issue for ten authored keys on a top-level report.

2. **Parity with the block table, as the card asked.** Command + output at head: block table (`:177-202`) and top-level table (`:276-305`) both count 17 `key: 'target'` entries, and a `diff` of the extracted entry lists prints "block and top-level tables identical in content and order". At merge-base the top-level table (`71ef221988:packages/spec/src/ui/report.zod.ts:265-274`) had 7 entries and lacked exactly the ten the card names. Every target is declared on `ReportSchema` at head: `dataset:336`, `rows:338`, `values:345`, `order:372`. None of the ten keys is a declared key (shape `:321-407`; `MetadataProtectionFields` contributes only `_lock`, `_lockReason`, `_lockSource`, `_provenance`, `_packageId`, `_packageVersion`, `_lockDocsUrl`), and the 17 `aliasProbe` forms are distinct, so alias-integrity claims 1 and 3 hold by reading; `Test Core` is green at head, which runs `alias-integrity.test.ts` unedited (PR #19789 holds that file, per the claim).

3. **Triage's first step was done and is consistent with the code.** The PR body records the pre-fix reading per key (9 no-suggestion, `orderBy` → `order` by distance, no wrong suggestion). I did not re-run it; it is consistent with the fallback budget at `suggestions.zod.ts:478` (`max(2, floor(len/3))`): folded `orderby` → `order` is distance 2 within budget 2; `sort` → `order` is distance 4 (DP computed) over budget 2; `object`, `metrics`, `measures`, `dimensions`, `groupings`, `groupBy`, `sortBy`, `objectName` have no declared key within budget. No `guidance` entry was needed: none of the ten has a reason to be refused at top level, so silence was the only wrong answer and it is gone. The comment above the ordering entries (`:298-301`) is true: `order` on a `joined` container is refused with the `blocks[]` pointer at `:425-432`.

4. **Rewritten comments are true.** "The block's three are wrong-layer pointers to keys this schema declares" (`:258-259`): block guidance `blocks`/`drilldown`/`protection` (`:207-212`) vs ReportSchema keys `blocks:394`, `drilldown:378`, `protection:402`; the block shape (`:216-241`) has no `drilldown`. The #5013 paragraph is byte-unchanged (head `:262-269` vs merge-base `:257-264`). The new history paragraph (`:271-275`) matches the measurement.

5. **Tests are weight-bearing.** `refs/review/pr-19855:packages/spec/src/ui/report.test.ts:265-333`: per-key rename pin ×10 (bears weight for 9 keys; the `orderBy` row is held by distance alone, which the PR itself states), advice-parses pin ×10 (preservation), and a parity pin derived from `strictObjectDeclarations()` with a non-vacuity floor over the ten and `silentOrDivergent` required empty — removing any one of the ten entries turns it red. The API it uses exists at `origin/main:packages/spec/src/shared/strict-object.ts:197-206` (`StrictObjectDeclaration { options, shape }`) and `:265` (export); the PR test imports it by relative path exactly as `alias-integrity.test.ts:125` does. `surface: 'this report'` is declared once in `packages/spec/src` (git grep at PR ref), so the exactly-one assertion holds.

6. **The platform-objects pin flip is correct and weight-bearing.** `refs/review/pr-19855:packages/platform-objects/src/apps/translations/report-form-echo-decisions.test.ts:634-652`. The old `it` asserted `not.toContain('Did you mean')` on top-level `measures` — the very defect the card names, recorded as a reading; keeping it would keep `Test Core (4/6)` red (it was red on `c78242fe05`, green at head, check-run 107169411613). The flip asserts `toContain('`measures` → `values`')`, which fails if the `measures` entry is removed from the top-level table (the pre-fix message was bare). It carries weight the spec test does not: this file imports `ReportSchema` from `@objectstack/spec/ui` (`:142`), i.e. the built dist, so it proves the shipped artifact carries the entry. The block half (`:645-651`) is unchanged. The header bullet rewrite (`:117-122`) is true, and the neighbouring bullets `:107-116` stay true (test `:601-607` still asserts `ReportSchema` refuses `measures`/`dimensions` with `unrecognized_keys`).

7. **Published prose: nothing goes false; one sentence becomes true.** `origin/main:content/docs/ui/reports.mdx:36-37` says writing `objectName`, `object`, `source` or `dataSet` "is rejected at authoring time with a pointer at `dataset`" — false for a top-level report at merge-base (table `:265-274` had only `dataSet`/`source`), true after this PR. `content/docs/data-modeling/analytics.mdx:235-240` (single-form removal) and `reports.mdx:105-108, 153-154` remain true. Docs-drift bot flagged only `analytics.mdx`, which needs no edit.

8. **Generated artifacts.** `origin/main:packages/spec/scripts/build-schemas.ts:1626-1665` reads only `options.guidance` from `strictObjectDeclarations()`, never `aliases`; `authorable-surface/ui.json` carries no alias keys. So no generated file is expected to move, matching the PR's `check:generated` claim and green `Lint & Repo Gates`.

9. **Missing vs the card's ask: nothing.** Beyond it: only the platform-objects flip, which is a necessary consequence (see ③).

### ② Semver level

`.changeset/19822-report-top-level-aliases.md` (blob `6388555f0c9`): `'@objectstack/spec': patch`, body line `Clause-②: no`, table of before/after per key, and the statement "Every accept/reject verdict is unchanged" — which ① confirms. AGENTS.md (`origin/main`) `:1082-1085`: a bug fix in a released package (`packages/spec/package.json` at main: `17.4.0`, `files[]` includes `dist` and `src/**/*.zod.ts`) takes `patch`; Clause-② asks whether the card widens the accept-set or enlarges the public surface (`scripts/pm/clause2-line.mjs:15-16`) — it does neither, so `no` is right and `patch` is the correct level. Not breaking: no `major`, no `**BREAKING` banner, no `(narrowing)` arm; `scripts/check-adr-0087-registration.mjs:631-640` raises no signal, and its own fixture at `:2255` lists precisely this shape (`patch` + bare `Clause-②: no`) under MUST_NOT_MATCH_BREAKING, so no ADR-0087 marker is required and the launch-window `minor` + BREAKING + marker rule does not apply. PR body carries the same `Clause-②: no` line-leading. `Check Changeset` green at head (both runs).

### ③ Boundary flags

- **non-blocking — file outside the claim's declared surface.** Claim 5793125463 declared `report.zod.ts` + the report tests beside it + generated files + `.changeset/`; the PR also edits `packages/platform-objects/src/apps/translations/report-form-echo-decisions.test.ts`. pm-dispatch `SKILL.md:314` (origin/main) says "stop on breach; explain in the report"; the round-2 os-dev-report (5795050403) explains it and the PR body was edited accordingly. `No other open PR may claim the same single-writer path` is green at head. Judged above as correct and weight-bearing.
- **non-blocking — pin not weight-bearing alone:** the `orderBy` row of the per-key rename pin (distance already reaches `order`); the PR declares this and the parity pin holds the entry.
- **non-blocking — CI measured against an older base than current main.** Check-runs at head ran on merge commit `a3d2e127db18cec1aba60725844cb99b5471553a` into `8cbc3c0084` (zod `^4.4.3`). `origin/main` `c1641868a3` since took zod `^4.6.1` and #19581's `markUnknownKeyRefusalTerminal` (`strict-object.ts`, 207-line delta after the CI base). The API the parity test uses is unchanged at current main (`:197-206`, `:265`); `suggestions.zod.ts` and `alias-probe.ts` are byte-identical merge-base to main; the four PR-touched files have no drift on main. Not re-run here per the review contract; the queue leg re-measures on landing.
- **non-blocking — dev-declared deviations:** (1) round-1 stale shared-checkout `with-fleet.sh` proxy 403 — no repo effect; (2) harness attribution trailer — all three commits carry the AGENTS.md `:452-453` model-free pair (`git log` output), and PR title/body/diff carry no model identifier (grep: none). The PR body ends with the session-URL footer plus a bare platform footer, which AGENTS.md `:449-450` attributes to the platform.
- **non-blocking — reporting gap:** the round-2 repo-wide prose search did not name `content/docs/ui/reports.mdx:36-37`, the one published sentence this behaviour change touches; it turns true, so no edit is needed.
- **non-blocking:** PR is still `draft: true`; `mergeable_state: clean`.
